name: agent-workspace-code-source-baseline
purpose: Records the local VS Code hard-fork source baseline, replay patch, validation commands, and dependency risk notes.

reader_guide.summary: Use this file before changing vscode-agent-workbench/source so the hard-fork base, branch, patch, and validation expectations stay explicit.
how_to_read: Confirm upstream.repository and upstream.commit before rebasing or refreshing the clone.
Confirm local_source.branch and local_source.commit before stacking new hard-fork commits.
Regenerate tracked_patch.path from the source commit after source changes.
Run validation.commands before considering a source slice ready.
update_triggers: The upstream VS Code source commit changes.
A new local source branch or hard-fork commit becomes the baseline.
The tracked patch path or patch generation command changes.
Validation commands, runtime versions, or dependency risk notes change.
Public distribution, signing, branding, or service endpoint gates are added.

reference_links.title: Differences between the repository and Visual Studio Code

structure_rules.rule: vscode-agent-workbench/source is a local nested clone and must stay ignored by the outer repository.
structure_rules.reason: The full VS Code checkout, dependencies, and build outputs are too large for the workspace repository and already have their own Git history.

structure_rules.rule: Each completed source slice must be represented by a source commit and a replayable patch under vscode-agent-workbench/patches.
structure_rules.reason: Patch tracking gives the outer workspace a durable artifact without vendoring the entire upstream repository.

field_guide.meaning: Pinned upstream source repository and commit used for this hard-fork slice.
Local branch and commit inside the ignored source clone.
Outer-repository patch artifact generated from the local source commit.
Commands already run and expected smoke checks for the baseline.
